verdict.rationale: Codex's own CLI docs say you can start it in a repository to explore unfamiliar code and plan a change, which matches finding where to start. They also describe inspecting files and splitting larger investigations across subagents. However, the evidence is brief feature-list text with no detail on how it explains architecture or structure. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of codebase-mapping or architecture-explanation output, independent or hands-on corroboration of codebase-understanding quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can understand how a codebase fits together to find where to start making changes

citations.quote: Start Codex in a repository to explore unfamiliar code, plan a change, edit files, and run your local development tools.
Inspect code, make changes, run commands, and automate repeatable work without leaving your terminal.
Let Codex inspect files, make edits, and run the tools already installed on your machine.
Split up a larger investigation — subagents: Ask Codex to delegate focused work to specialized agents, then bring their findings back into the main terminal session.
